questions.q: Which polysaccharide is built from β-D-glucose units and gives cellobiose on partial hydrolysis?
questions.explain: Cellulose is an unbranched β(1→4) polymer of glucose, and cellobiose is its β(1→4) disaccharide unit. Amylose, amylopectin and glycogen are all α-glucose polymers.

questions.q: The correct increasing order of branching is:
questions.explain: Amylose has no branches, amylopectin branches about every 25–30 glucose units and glycogen about every 8–12 units, so glycogen is the most branched.

questions.q: Which statement about starch is correct?
options: Amylose is the water-soluble component with only α(1→4) links
Amylopectin is the water-soluble component and gives a deep blue colour with iodine
Amylose forms about 80–85% of starch and is branched through C1–C6 links
Diastase converts starch directly into glucose
questions.explain: Amylose (about 15–20% of starch) is the unbranched, water-soluble, α(1→4)-linked component that gives the blue iodine colour. Diastase gives maltose; maltase is needed to reach glucose.

questions.q: Cattle can digest cellulose but humans cannot. The best explanation is:
options: Cattle produce the enzyme cellulase in their own digestive glands
Microorganisms in the rumen produce cellulase that hydrolyses β-glycosidic bonds
Cellulose in grass contains α(1→4) links, unlike cotton cellulose
Cattle have diastase that converts cellulose into maltose
questions.explain: Humans lack an enzyme for β-glycosidic bonds; in ruminants it is the gut bacteria, not the animal itself, that produce cellulase. Option A is the common trap.
